title: Oregon Family Claims Massive UFO Hovered Outside Daughter's Bedroom Window, Then They Fell Sick
excerpt: ufo flying saucer An Oregon family said they saw a large UFO hovering outside their home that appeared to change shape before it vanished into thin air.
content:
An Oregon family said they saw a large UFO hovering outside their home that appeared to change shape before it vanished into thin air. They also say two members of the family fell ill after the encounter.

The mother, who asked to be identified only as “S,” said she first noticed something strange at about 8 p.m. while sitting on her back patio, according to the Daily Mail. Then, about an hour later, things got even weirder.

“I saw what looked like something I’ve never seen fall out of the sky. Almost like a bird was shot dead in the air and plummeted,” she wrote in her report. “The object went from looking rectangular to a large ball, then a small ball in a matter of a blink. I pointed out to my partner and daughter, ‘There’s something falling out of the sky!'”

The alleged UFO sighting, which took place in Wilsonville, Oregon, was recently reported to the National UFO Reporting Center (NUFORC).

Family Says UFO Was As Wide As Three Airplanes

The woman’s 12-year-old daughter saw bright lights flashing outside her window and came running out of her bedroom around 9:14 p.m. Her parents went to check it out and reportedly saw a huge silver object hovering near their home.

The family described the UFO as partially transparent, with two very bright lights. The daughter estimated that it was as wide as three airplanes. She also managed to photograph it.

“It hovered there for almost a minute and then just disappeared!” the mother reported. “My daughter was looking at it before she got us and said it looked like it was see-through silver when it got close.”

As if that wasn’t weird enough, the mother and daughter reportedly began to experience physical symptoms after the incident. The mother reported feeling nauseous and having difficulty maintaining her balance, and her daughter experienced headaches throughout the night.

Thankfully, both of them reportedly felt better the next day.

UFO Investigator Couldn’t Explain The Sighting

NUFORC investigator Keith Bickford investigated the family’s claims and contacted two local farmers who use agricultural drones in the area. Neither reported flying drones anywhere near the size of the object the family described.

“Both the Clackamas County Sheriff’s Office and the Wilsonville Police Department had no UAP or UFO reports for that evening. “FlightRadar24 showed nothing,” Bickford wrote. Ultimately, he classified the incident as an anomalous sighting.

However, the report in Oregon follows a resurgence of interest in UFOs after the Pentagon released files on a mysterious triangular aircraft and allegations surrounding Roswell, and a report of a mysterious “jellyfish” UFO spotted near an Alaska military base then vanished without a trace went viral.

President Donald Trump also recently weighed in on reports from military pilots who said they saw UFOs that could outrun fighter jets.

Meanwhile, a former Pentagon UFO investigator claims the U.S. government has videos of mysterious aircraft that it still hasn’t released to the public, including one showing a triangular craft hovering over a nuclear missile facility.

Jay Stratton, who helped establish the Pentagon’s Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (UAP) Task Force, recently discussed his years of investigating UFOs and what he believes the government still keeps secret.

“I know there’s more to the story that’s not being put out there,” he said.
